column71: In the screens that follow, you will be asked about therapies for Plaque Psoriasis patients.Please consider the following definitions when responding to questions throughout the remainder of the screener and the survey:Prescription Steroidal Topical Therapy This includes all steroid-based topical therapies that require a prescription and does not include over the counter (OTC) topicals. These include:Mild / Least Potent – Hydrocortisone 1% powderMid-Strength -Aristocort A 0.1% (triamcinolone topical), Cloderm (clocortolone), Elocon Cream (mometasone), Kenalog Ointment (triamcinolone acetonide), Synalar Ointment (fluocinolone), Valisone (betamethasone valerate)Upper Mid-Strength - Lidex-E (fluocinonide), Topicort-LP (desoximetasone)Potent - ApexiCon E (diflorasone diacetate), Elocon Ointment (mometasone), Halog (halcinonide), Topicort (desoximetasone)High Potency - Clobex (clobetasol propionate), Olux E (clobetasol propionate foam), Psorcon (diflorasone diacetate cream USP), Temovate E (clobetasol propionate emollient cream), Ultravate (halobetasol propionate), Vanos (fluocinonide)Novel Non-Steroidal Topical TherapyThis includes recently launched prescription topicals that are not steroid based. These include:Vtama (tapinarof)Zoryve (roflumilast)Systemic Therapy Systemic therapy for Plaque Psoriasis refer to both conventional oral DMARDs as well as advanced orals and biologics. Systemic therapies include:Conventional oral DMARDs – prednisone, methotrexate, leflunomide and sulfasalazineAdvanced oral therapies – Otezla (apremilast), Sotyktu (deucravacitinib)and Icotyde (icotrokinra)Advanced injectable biologicAnti-TNF agents [Enbrel, Humira (adalimumab) and biosimiliars , Remicade, Cimzia, Simponi]IL-17s [Cosentyx, Taltz, Siliq, Bimzelx]IL-23s [Skyrizi, Tremfya, Ilumya]IL-23s / IL-12s [Stelara]
